A1_signal_density.why: Concise and practical, but limited deeper analysis beyond short descriptions and action verbs.

A2_source_integrity.why: All links point to primary GitHub/Hugging Face pages and resolved; one numeric claim (Gradio stars “over 43k”) appears slightly off vs the repo page.

A3_focus_alignment.why: The set is coherent around practical ML tooling/datasets without obvious drift.

A4_delta_clarity.why: The “New today” block clearly separates newly trending items from the watch-list.

A5_coverage.why: Given the quiet window, coverage is adequate but no additional missed stories were added from the last 24 hours.

X1_board_legibility.why: The lead item (Gradio) clearly signals the theme (practical ML tooling) and the list is easy to scan.

X2_instrument_honesty.why: Traction signals are used with some caveats; improving provenance and exactness of numeric claims would raise trust.

X3_freshness.why: Digest commit time indicates it is well under 6 hours old at evaluation time.

X4_failure_surface.why: Per-file contract loading and freshness-by-commit-time reduce cascade risk, but the need for a recovery run highlights remaining surface area.

X5_coupling.why: No evidence of cross-boundary coupling; eval artifacts are separate from digest generation.

notes.recovery_prefix_text: Recovery run for 2026-07-11. This morning's scheduled run escalated on a contract-load stderr false alarm; PR #26 landed the fix (git-commit-time freshness, per-file load, explicit gh CLI usage) and this run produces today's eval.
